name: FOREST_LIST_COLORING_TERMINAL

external_authority.reference: Jansen and Scheffler, Generalized coloring for tree-like graphs
external_authority.result: List Coloring on trees is solvable in linear time; partial k-trees polynomially.

external_authority.reference: Lampis lecture notes, Exact Algorithms, Theorem 4
external_authority.result: List Coloring can be solved in polynomial time on trees; repeated singleton propagation followed by the forest >=2-list rule is correct.

terminal_definition.input: A forest F with arbitrary finite vertex color lists L(v).
algorithm: Repeat exact singleton propagation: if L(v)={c}, fix v=c and remove c from every neighbor list.
If an empty list appears, return UNSAT with the empty-list certificate.
When no singleton remains, every remaining list has size at least 2.
Each remaining forest component is list-colorable: delete a leaf, color the smaller forest inductively, then choose for the leaf a list color different from its at-most-one colored neighbor.
Reconstruct propagated singleton assignments in reverse order.

alternative_DP.state: F(v)={c in L(v): for every child u there exists d in F(u) with d!=c}.
alternative_DP.criterion: A tree is list-colorable iff F(root) is nonempty.
alternative_DP.complexity_with_four_colors: O(|V|+|E|) up to a constant factor depending only on the four-color palette.

target_claims: Arbitrary-list coloring on forests is polynomial-time solvable.
For a fixed four-color palette, the terminal is linear-time up to a constant factor.
The terminal needs no P7-free assumption.
Its use after fixed-boundary propagation is exact provided all boundary restrictions have been incorporated into lists.
forbidden: Infer anything about cyclic residual components.
Treat forest recognition alone as a coloring answer without exact lists.
